q: A railway servant dies while in service after completing 4 years of qualifying service. His emoluments at the time of his death are Rs 36,000 per month. The death gratuity payable to his family, at six times the emoluments, as admissible for this length of service, will be:
e: Under the RS (Pension) Rules death gratuity slab, service of 1 to 5 years earns 6 times emoluments. Here service is 4 years, so gratuity = 6 x Rs 36,000 = Rs 2,16,000.

q: Under Section 21 of the Factories Act, 1948, applicable to staff employed in railway workshops, in every factory, every dangerous part of any machinery shall be:

options.A: Painted red to warn the workers
options.B: Securely fenced, so as to render it safe so long as the fenced part is in motion or in use
options.C: Operated only by the foreman of the shop
options.D: Covered with a notice board displaying the danger involved

e: Section 21 of the Factories Act, 1948 requires every dangerous part of machinery to be securely fenced so as to render it safe so long as the fenced part is in motion or in use; mere painting or notice boards do not satisfy the section.

q: Under Section 8(2) of the Right to Information Act, 2005, a public authority may allow access to information, notwithstanding the exemptions contained in the Act and the provisions of the Official Secrets Act, 1923, if:

options.A: The applicant pays an additional fee for such disclosure
options.B: The applicant is a Member of Parliament
options.C: The information is more than ten years old
options.D: Public interest in disclosure of the information outweighs the harm to the protected interests

e: Section 8(2) of the RTI Act, 2005 gives the Act overriding effect: access may be allowed even over the exemptions and the Official Secrets Act, 1923 where public interest in disclosure outweighs the harm to the protected interests.

q: Under Section 9 of the Trade Unions Act, 1926, the certificate of registration issued by the Registrar to a registered trade union of railway servants shall be:

options.A: Conclusive evidence that the trade union has been duly registered under the Act
options.B: Evidence only of the date on which the application for registration was made
options.C: Valid only for a period of one year from the date of its issue
options.D: Mere proof of the identity of the office-bearers of the trade union

e: Section 9 of the Trade Unions Act, 1926 makes the certificate of registration conclusive evidence that the trade union has been duly registered under the Act; it is not mere proof of identity or valid for only one year.

q: A railway servant dies while in service after completing 26 years of qualifying service. His emoluments at the time of his death are Rs 42,000 per month. The death gratuity payable to his family, at half a month's emoluments for each completed six-monthly period of qualifying service, will be:
e: For death after 20 years, death gratuity is half a month's emoluments for each completed six-monthly period, subject to a maximum of 33 times emoluments. 26 years = 52 periods, so 52 x Rs 21,000 = Rs 10,92,000, which is within the 33 x cap.

q: Under Section 8 of the Payment of Bonus Act, 1965, an employee becomes eligible for bonus under the Act if he has worked in the establishment during an accounting year for:

options.A: Not less than 240 days
options.B: Not less than 180 days
options.C: Not less than 30 working days
options.D: The whole of the accounting year, without any break

e: Section 8 of the Payment of Bonus Act, 1965 fixes eligibility at working for not less than 30 working days in the accounting year; the higher day thresholds in the other options do not apply to bonus eligibility.

q: Under Rule 3A of the Railway Services (Conduct) Rules, 1966, relating to promptness and courtesy, no railway servant shall:

options.A: In the performance of his official duties, act in a discourteous manner or adopt dilatory tactics, or wilfully cause delays, in the disposal of the work entrusted to him
options.B: Attend office on a holiday when called upon to do so
options.C: Accept a verbal order from his superior officer in an emergency
options.D: Discuss official matters with his colleagues in the office

e: Rule 3A of the RS (Conduct) Rules, 1966 bars a railway servant from acting discourteously, adopting dilatory tactics or wilfully causing delays in disposal of work entrusted to him, in the performance of official duties.

q: Under Section 8 of the Employees' Compensation Act, 1923, compensation payable in respect of the death of an employee, or to a woman or a person under a legal disability, shall be:

options.A: Paid by the employer directly to the dependants, as he considers fit
options.B: Deposited with the Commissioner, and distributed by the Commissioner among the dependants in accordance with the provisions of the Act
options.C: Retained by the employer until the dependants obtain a succession certificate
options.D: Credited to the Staff Benefit Fund of the establishment

e: Section 8 of the Employees' Compensation Act, 1923 requires compensation for death, or payable to a woman or a person under legal disability, to be deposited with the Commissioner, who distributes it among the dependants; the employer cannot pay it directly as he pleases.

q: Under Section 48 of the Factories Act, 1948, applicable to staff employed in railway workshops, a suitable room for the use of children under the age of six years of women workers (a creche) shall be provided and maintained in every factory wherein:

options.A: More than 100 women workers are ordinarily employed
options.B: More than 50 women workers are ordinarily employed
options.C: More than 250 workers are ordinarily employed
options.D: More than 30 women workers are ordinarily employed

e: Section 48 of the Factories Act, 1948 requires a creche for children under six years of women workers in every factory wherein more than 30 women workers are ordinarily employed.

q: A railway servant retires on superannuation after rendering 33 years of qualifying service. His emoluments at the time of retirement are Rs 60,000 per month. The retirement gratuity payable to him, at one-fourth of a month's emoluments for each completed six-monthly period of qualifying service, subject to the prescribed maximum, will be:
e: Retirement gratuity is one-fourth of emoluments per completed six-monthly period, capped at 16.5 times emoluments. 33 years = 66 periods, so 66 x Rs 15,000 = Rs 9,90,000, which equals the 16.5 x Rs 60,000 maximum.

q: Under Section 20(1) of the Right to Information Act, 2005, where the Central Information Commission is of the opinion that the Central Public Information Officer has, without any reasonable cause, refused to receive an application for information or has not furnished the information within the prescribed time, it shall impose a penalty of:

options.A: Rs 100 for each day of default, subject to a maximum of Rs 10,000
options.B: Rs 250 for each day till the application is received or the information is furnished, so however that the total amount of such penalty shall not exceed Rs 25,000
options.C: Rs 500 for each day of default, subject to a maximum of Rs 50,000
options.D: A lump sum penalty of Rs 25,000 in every case

e: Section 20(1) of the RTI Act, 2005 prescribes a penalty of Rs 250 for each day till the application is received or information furnished, subject to a total maximum of Rs 25,000, for refusal or delay without reasonable cause.

q: Under Rule 18 of the Railway Servants (Discipline and Appeal) Rules, 1968, where two or more railway servants are involved in the same disciplinary case, the competent authority may direct that:

options.A: Each railway servant shall be proceeded against separately in all cases
options.B: The case shall be transferred to the Railway Board for decision
options.C: Disciplinary proceedings against all of them be taken in a common proceeding
options.D: Only the senior-most railway servant among them shall be proceeded against

e: Rule 18 of the RS (Discipline and Appeal) Rules, 1968 permits the competent authority, where two or more railway servants are involved in the same case, to direct that disciplinary proceedings against all of them be taken in a common proceeding.

q: Under Section 10 of the Payment of Bonus Act, 1965, the minimum bonus payable by an employer to his employees in an accounting year is:

options.A: 8.33 per cent of the salary or wage earned by the employee during the accounting year, payable whether or not the employer has any allocable surplus in that year
options.B: 5 per cent of the salary or wage earned by the employee during the accounting year
options.C: 8.33 per cent of the net profit of the establishment for the accounting year
options.D: Payable only in a year in which the employer has earned a profit

e: Section 10 of the Payment of Bonus Act, 1965 fixes minimum bonus at 8.33 per cent of the salary or wage earned during the accounting year, payable whether or not the employer has any allocable surplus in that year.

q: Under Section 67 of the Factories Act, 1948, applicable to staff employed in railway workshops, no child shall be required or allowed to work in any factory if he has not completed his:

options.A: Twelfth year
options.B: Sixteenth year
options.C: Fourteenth year
options.D: Eighteenth year

e: Section 67 of the Factories Act, 1948 prohibits employment in a factory of a child who has not completed his fourteenth year.

q: A railway servant retires on superannuation after rendering 15 years of qualifying service. His emoluments at the time of retirement are Rs 36,000 per month. The retirement gratuity payable to him, at one-fourth of a month's emoluments for each completed six-monthly period of qualifying service, will be:
e: Retirement gratuity is one-fourth of emoluments per completed six-monthly period. 15 years = 30 periods, so 30 x Rs 9,000 (one-fourth of Rs 36,000) = Rs 2,70,000, within the 16.5 times maximum.

q: Under Section 24 of the Trade Unions Act, 1926, two or more registered trade unions may become amalgamated as one trade union only if:

options.A: The Registrar of Trade Unions passes an order directing the amalgamation
options.B: All the members of the unions concerned agree to the amalgamation unanimously
options.C: The votes of at least one-half of the members of each union entitled to vote are recorded, and at least sixty per cent of the votes so recorded are in favour of the proposal
options.D: A simple majority of the office-bearers of each union passes a resolution to that effect

e: Section 24 of the Trade Unions Act, 1926 permits amalgamation only if votes of at least one-half of the members of each union entitled to vote are recorded and at least 60 per cent of the votes so recorded favour the proposal.

q: Under Section 6 of the Payment of Wages Act, 1936, all wages payable to an employed person shall be paid:

options.A: Only in cash, in current coin
options.B: Only by cheque drawn in favour of the employed person
options.C: In kind, in the form of articles of daily use
options.D: In current coin or currency notes, or by cheque, or by crediting the wages to his bank account

e: Section 6 of the Payment of Wages Act, 1936 requires wages to be paid in current coin or currency notes, or by cheque, or by crediting the wages to the bank account of the employed person.

q:
Consider the following statements regarding gratuity under the Payment of Gratuity Act, 1972:
1. Gratuity is payable to an employee on the termination of his employment after he has rendered continuous service of not less than five years.
2. The condition of completion of five years of continuous service does not apply where the termination of employment is due to the death or disablement of the employee.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: 2 only
options.C: Both 1 and 2
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

e: Both statements are correct under the Payment of Gratuity Act, 1972: gratuity normally needs not less than five years of continuous service, but that condition does not apply where termination is due to death or disablement of the employee.

q: Under Section 14 of the Employees' Compensation Act, 1923, where an employee, who has given notice of an accident, refuses without reasonable cause to submit himself for medical examination by a qualified medical practitioner, when so required, or in any way obstructs the same:

options.A: His right to compensation shall be suspended during the continuance of such refusal or obstruction
options.B: He shall be dismissed from the service of the employer
options.C: He shall forfeit his right to compensation permanently
options.D: The employer shall become liable to pay double the amount of compensation

e: Section 14 of the Employees' Compensation Act, 1923 suspends the right to compensation during the continuance of an unjustified refusal to submit to, or obstruction of, a required medical examination; it is suspension, not permanent forfeiture or dismissal.

q: Under Section 44 of the Factories Act, 1948, applicable to staff employed in railway workshops, in every factory, suitable arrangements shall be made for workers who are obliged to work standing, so that:

options.A: They are not required to stand for more than two hours at a time
options.B: Their hours of work are reduced by one hour every day
options.C: They are provided with a chair at their place of work in all cases
options.D: They may take advantage of any opportunities for resting which may occur in the course of their work, by providing suitable facilities for sitting

e: Section 44 of the Factories Act, 1948 requires suitable arrangements for sitting to be provided and maintained for workers obliged to work standing, so that they may take advantage of opportunities for resting in the course of their work.

q: A railway servant retires from service after rendering 6 years of qualifying service and is accordingly not entitled to pension. His emoluments at the time of retirement are Rs 44,000 per month. The service gratuity payable to him, at half a month's emoluments for each completed six-monthly period of qualifying service, will be:
e: Service gratuity for a retiree not entitled to pension is half a month's emoluments per completed six-monthly period. 6 years = 12 periods, so 12 x Rs 22,000 = Rs 2,64,000.

q: Under Section 19(5) of the Right to Information Act, 2005, in any appeal proceedings under the Act, the onus to prove that a denial of a request for information was justified shall be on:

options.A: The applicant who made the request for information
options.B: The Central Public Information Officer who denied the request
options.C: The First Appellate Authority
options.D: The public authority holding the information

e: Section 19(5) of the RTI Act, 2005 places the onus of proving that a denial of a request was justified on the Central Public Information Officer who denied the request, not on the applicant.

q: Under Section 27 of the Trade Unions Act, 1926, notice of the dissolution of a registered trade union of railway servants, signed by seven members and by the Secretary of the trade union, shall be sent to the Registrar of Trade Unions within:

options.A: Seven days of the dissolution
options.B: Thirty days of the dissolution
options.C: Three months of the dissolution
options.D: Fourteen days of the dissolution

e: Section 27 of the Trade Unions Act, 1926 requires notice of dissolution, signed by seven members and the Secretary, to be sent to the Registrar within fourteen days of the dissolution.

q: Under Section 4(6) of the Payment of Gratuity Act, 1972, the gratuity of an employee may be forfeited, wholly or partially, where:

options.A: The employee resigns from service before completing ten years of service
options.B: His services have been terminated for any act, wilful omission or negligence causing any damage or loss to, or destruction of, the property belonging to the employer, or for riotous conduct, or for an offence involving moral turpitude
options.C: The employee remains on unauthorised absence from duty
options.D: The employer has suffered a loss in business during the year

e: Section 4(6) of the Payment of Gratuity Act, 1972 permits forfeiture, wholly or partly, where services are terminated for an act, wilful omission or negligence causing damage or loss to employer property, riotous conduct, or an offence involving moral turpitude.

q: Under Section 41B of the Factories Act, 1948, applicable to staff employed in railway workshops, the occupier of every factory involving a hazardous process shall:

options.A: Disclose all information regarding dangers, including health hazards, and the measures to overcome them, to the workers employed in the factory, the local authority and the general public in the vicinity
options.B: Keep all information regarding the hazardous process strictly confidential
options.C: Disclose such information only to the Chief Inspector of Factories
options.D: Disclose such information only after an accident has occurred in the factory

e: Section 41B of the Factories Act, 1948 obliges the occupier of a factory involving a hazardous process to disclose all information on dangers, health hazards and measures to overcome them to the workers, the local authority and the general public in the vicinity.

q: The last basic pay drawn by a deceased railway servant was Rs 46,000 per month. The family pension payable to his family at the normal rate, at 30 per cent of the last basic pay drawn, will be:

options.A: Rs 23,000 per month
options.B: Rs 9,200 per month
options.C: Rs 13,800 per month
options.D: Rs 15,333 per month

e: Normal rate family pension under the RS (Pension) Rules is 30 per cent of last basic pay. 30 per cent of Rs 46,000 = Rs 13,800 per month; 50 per cent would be the enhanced rate, not the normal rate.

q: Under Section 30 of the Employees' Compensation Act, 1923, an appeal against specified orders of a Commissioner under the Act, involving a substantial question of law, lies to the High Court, and must be preferred within a period of:

options.A: 30 days
options.B: 60 days
options.C: 90 days
options.D: 45 days

e: Section 30 of the Employees' Compensation Act, 1923 allows an appeal to the High Court on a substantial question of law against specified orders of a Commissioner, and it must be preferred within 60 days.

q: Under Section 11 of the Payment of Bonus Act, 1965, where the allocable surplus of an establishment in an accounting year exceeds the amount of the minimum bonus payable, the employer shall pay bonus to every employee in proportion to the salary or wage earned by him during the year, subject to a maximum of:

options.A: 8.33 per cent of the salary or wage earned
options.B: 10 per cent of the salary or wage earned
options.C: 15 per cent of the salary or wage earned
options.D: 20 per cent of the salary or wage earned

e: Section 11 of the Payment of Bonus Act, 1965 caps bonus, where allocable surplus exceeds the minimum bonus, at 20 per cent of the salary or wage earned by the employee during the accounting year.

q: Under Section 10 of the Trade Unions Act, 1926, the Registrar of Trade Unions may withdraw or cancel the certificate of registration of a registered trade union of railway servants if he is satisfied that:

options.A: The trade union has passed a resolution criticising the Railway Administration
options.B: The certificate of registration has been obtained by fraud or mistake, or the trade union has ceased to exist, or has wilfully contravened a provision of the Act after notice from the Registrar
options.C: The membership of the trade union has fallen below one thousand
options.D: The office-bearers of the trade union have completed their term of office

e: Section 10 of the Trade Unions Act, 1926 lets the Registrar withdraw or cancel registration where the certificate was obtained by fraud or mistake, the union has ceased to exist, or it has wilfully contravened a provision of the Act after notice from the Registrar.

q: Under Rule 21 of the Railway Servants (Discipline and Appeal) Rules, 1968, which prescribes a special procedure in certain cases, the procedure of holding an inquiry may be dispensed with where:

options.A: The charged railway servant requests in writing that no inquiry be held
options.B: The disciplinary authority is of the opinion that the inquiry will take a long time
options.C: A penalty is imposed on a railway servant on the ground of conduct which has led to his conviction on a criminal charge, or the authority is satisfied, for reasons to be recorded in writing, that it is not reasonably practicable to hold an inquiry, or that in the interest of the security of the State it is not expedient to hold an inquiry
options.D: The penalty proposed to be imposed is only a minor penalty

e: Rule 21 of the RS (Discipline and Appeal) Rules, 1968 dispenses with inquiry where penalty follows conviction on a criminal charge, or the authority records in writing that holding an inquiry is not reasonably practicable, or that it is inexpedient in the interest of the security of the State.

q: Under Section 31 of the Factories Act, 1948, applicable to staff employed in railway workshops, where, in any factory, any part of a machine or any plant is operated at a pressure above the atmospheric pressure, effective measures shall be taken to ensure that:

options.A: The safe working pressure of such part is not exceeded
options.B: Such part is operated only during the day shift
options.C: Such part is painted with heat-resistant paint
options.D: A separate register is maintained for such part by the Accounts Office

e: Section 31 of the Factories Act, 1948 requires effective measures to ensure that the safe working pressure of any part of a machine or plant operated above atmospheric pressure is not exceeded.

q: Under Section 15 of the Trade Unions Act, 1926, the general funds of a registered trade union of railway servants may be spent on:

options.A: The payment of donations to a political party
options.B: Loans to persons who are not members of the trade union
options.C: The purchase of shares of private companies by way of investment
options.D: The conduct of trade disputes on behalf of the trade union or its members, and the payment of compensation to members for loss arising out of trade disputes

e: Section 15 of the Trade Unions Act, 1926 permits general funds to be spent on the conduct of trade disputes on behalf of the union or its members and on compensation to members for loss arising out of trade disputes; political donations come from a separate political fund.

q: Under Section 19 of the Payment of Bonus Act, 1965, all amounts payable to an employee by way of bonus under the Act shall be paid in cash by the employer within:

options.A: One month of the close of the accounting year
options.B: Three months of the close of the accounting year
options.C: Eight months of the close of the accounting year
options.D: Twelve months of the close of the accounting year

e: Section 19 of the Payment of Bonus Act, 1965 requires all bonus amounts payable to be paid in cash within eight months of the close of the accounting year.

q: Under Section 13 of the Payment of Gratuity Act, 1972, gratuity payable to an employee under the Act shall:

options.A: Be liable to attachment in execution of a decree of a civil court, like any other amount due to him
options.B: Not be liable to attachment in execution of any decree or order of any civil, revenue or criminal court
options.C: Be liable to attachment only at the instance of the employer
options.D: Be liable to attachment only for the recovery of Government dues

e: Section 13 of the Payment of Gratuity Act, 1972 protects gratuity from attachment in execution of any decree or order of any civil, revenue or criminal court.

q: Under Section 21 of the Apprentices Act, 1961, on the successful completion of the apprenticeship training, an Act Apprentice engaged in a railway workshop is granted:

options.A: A degree in the trade in which he was trained
options.B: A certificate of proficiency in the trade by the employer
options.C: An appointment letter for a regular post in the workshop
options.D: A National Apprenticeship Certificate by the National Council, after passing the test conducted for the purpose

e: Section 21 of the Apprentices Act, 1961 provides that an apprentice who passes the test conducted by the National Council on completion of training is granted a National Apprenticeship Certificate by the National Council; it is not a degree or an appointment letter from the employer.

q: Under Section 61 of the Factories Act, 1948, applicable to staff employed in railway workshops, a notice of periods of work for adult workers, in the prescribed form, showing clearly the periods during which adult workers may be required to work, shall be:

options.A: Displayed in a conspicuous place in the factory by the manager, and a duplicate copy thereof sent by him to the Inspector of Factories
options.B: Maintained only in the personal file of the manager of the factory
options.C: Sent by the manager to the Railway Board every month
options.D: Displayed only in the office of the Inspector of Factories

e: Section 61 of the Factories Act, 1948 requires the notice of periods of work for adult workers to be displayed in a conspicuous place in the factory by the manager, with a duplicate copy sent to the Inspector of Factories.

q: Under Section 15 of the Payment of Wages Act, 1936, an application in respect of a claim arising out of a deduction from wages, or delay in the payment of wages, shall ordinarily be presented to the Authority appointed under the Act within:

options.A: Three months from the date of the deduction or the date on which the payment was due
options.B: Six months from the date of the deduction or the date on which the payment was due
options.C: Twelve months from the date of the deduction or the date on which the payment was due
options.D: Two years from the date of the deduction or the date on which the payment was due

e: Section 15 of the Payment of Wages Act, 1936 requires a claim application for deduction from wages or delayed payment to be presented within twelve months from the date of deduction or the date payment was due.

q: Under Section 22 of the Apprentices Act, 1961, in regard to the employment of an apprentice after the completion of his apprenticeship training in a railway workshop:

options.A: It is obligatory on the employer to offer him employment in the workshop
options.B: He is entitled, as a matter of right, to appointment against a regular vacancy
options.C: He must be absorbed against the first vacancy arising in the trade
options.D: It shall not be obligatory on the part of the employer to offer any employment to the apprentice, nor shall it be obligatory on the part of the apprentice to accept an employment offered to him

e: Section 22 of the Apprentices Act, 1961 expressly provides it is not obligatory on the employer to offer employment to an apprentice after training, nor on the apprentice to accept employment offered to him.

q: Under Section 26 of the Factories Act, 1948, applicable to staff employed in railway workshops, in every factory, every set screw, bolt or key on any revolving shaft, spindle, wheel or pinion, and all spur, worm and other toothed or friction gearing in motion, which does not require frequent adjustment while in motion, shall be:

options.A: Painted in a bright colour
options.B: Sunk, encased or otherwise effectively guarded so as to prevent danger
options.C: Removed before the machinery is started
options.D: Marked with the name of the manufacturer

e: Section 26 of the Factories Act, 1948 requires every set screw, bolt or key on a revolving shaft, spindle, wheel or pinion, and toothed or friction gearing in motion not requiring frequent adjustment, to be sunk, encased or otherwise effectively guarded so as to prevent danger.

q: Deputation (Duty) Allowance admissible to a railway servant on deputation to another post, where the deputation is at the same station, is payable at the rate of:

options.A: 5 per cent of his basic pay, subject to a maximum of Rs 5,625 per month
options.B: 10 per cent of his basic pay, subject to a maximum of Rs 9,000 per month
options.C: 5 per cent of his basic pay, without any ceiling
options.D: A fixed amount of Rs 2,000 per month in all cases

e: Deputation (Duty) Allowance is 5% of basic pay (same station) / 10% (change of station), with operative ceilings of Rs 5,625 / Rs 11,250 per month - the base caps of Rs 4,500 / Rs 9,000 (DoPT OM No. 2/11/2017-Estt.(Pay-II) dated 24.11.2017) stand enhanced by 25% since DA reached 50%. (Source: MoF DA OM No. 1/1/2024-E-II(B) dated 12.03.2024; DoPT consolidated deputation guidelines OM dated 28.03.2024; effective 01.01.2024.)

q: Under Section 3 of the Industrial Disputes Act, 1947, a Works Committee, consisting of representatives of the employer and of the workmen engaged in the establishment, with the number of representatives of the workmen not being less than that of the employer, is required to be constituted in an industrial establishment in which:

options.A: Fifty or more workmen are employed
options.B: One hundred or more workmen are employed or have been employed on any day in the preceding twelve months
options.C: Five hundred or more workmen are employed
options.D: One thousand or more workmen are employed

e: Section 3 of the Industrial Disputes Act, 1947 requires a Works Committee in an industrial establishment in which 100 or more workmen are employed or have been employed on any day in the preceding twelve months, with workmen's representatives not less than the employer's.

q: Children Education Allowance admissible to a railway servant in respect of a Divyang child is reimbursed at:

options.A: The normal rate admissible for other children
options.B: One and a half times the normal rate
options.C: Double the normal rate, that is, Rs 5,625 per month
options.D: Three times the normal rate

e: Children Education Allowance for a Divyang child is reimbursed at double the normal rate. With the normal rate at Rs 2,812.50 per month after the DA-linked revision, double works out to Rs 5,625 per month.

q: Night Duty Allowance under the 7th CPC dispensation is admissible to eligible non-gazetted railway servants drawing basic pay up to:

options.A: Rs 43,600 per month
options.B: Rs 50,000 per month
options.C: Rs 36,700 per month
options.D: There is no ceiling of basic pay for its admissibility

e: Under the 7th CPC dispensation, Night Duty Allowance is admissible to eligible non-gazetted railway servants drawing basic pay up to Rs 43,600 per month; staff above that ceiling are not eligible.

q: Under Section 25F of the Industrial Disputes Act, 1947, a workman who has been in continuous service for not less than one year shall not be retrenched until he has been given one month's notice in writing, or wages in lieu of such notice, and compensation equivalent to:

options.A: Fifteen days' average pay for every completed year of continuous service, or any part thereof in excess of six months
options.B: One month's average pay for every completed year of continuous service
options.C: Seven days' average pay for every completed year of continuous service
options.D: Thirty days' average pay for every completed year of continuous service

e: Section 25F of the Industrial Disputes Act, 1947 requires, before retrenchment of a workman with not less than one year of continuous service, one month's notice or wages in lieu, plus compensation equal to fifteen days' average pay for every completed year of continuous service or part thereof in excess of six months.

q: A Kit Pass issued to a railway servant who is transferred in public interest entitles him to:

options.A: Travel in a higher class than his entitlement, with his family
options.B: Convey his personal effects and luggage by train in connection with his transfer, in accordance with the prescribed entitlement
options.C: Retain his railway quarter at the old station free of rent for one year
options.D: Draw an advance equal to one month's pay for the purchase of luggage

e: A Kit Pass on transfer in public interest entitles the railway servant to convey his personal effects and luggage by train in connection with the transfer, as per the prescribed entitlement under the Pass Rules.

q: A railway servant dies while in service after completing 7 years of qualifying service. His emoluments at the time of his death are Rs 54,000 per month. The death gratuity payable to his family, at twelve times the emoluments as admissible for this length of service, will be:
e: For death in service with 5 to 11 years of service, the death gratuity slab is 12 times emoluments. Here service is 7 years, so gratuity = 12 x Rs 54,000 = Rs 6,48,000.

q: A railway servant dies while in service after completing 18 years of qualifying service. His emoluments at the time of his death are Rs 56,000 per month. The death gratuity payable to his family, at twenty times the emoluments as admissible for this length of service, will be:
e: For death in service with 11 to 20 years of service, the death gratuity slab is 20 times emoluments. Here service is 18 years, so gratuity = 20 x Rs 56,000 = Rs 11,20,000.

q: A railway servant retires on superannuation after rendering 29 years of qualifying service. His emoluments at the time of retirement are Rs 48,000 per month. The retirement gratuity payable to him, at one-fourth of a month's emoluments for each completed six-monthly period of qualifying service, will be:
e: Retirement gratuity is one-fourth of emoluments per completed six-monthly period. 29 years = 58 periods, so 58 x Rs 12,000 (one-fourth of Rs 48,000) = Rs 6,96,000, within the 16.5 times maximum of Rs 7,92,000.

q: A railway servant retires from service after rendering 3 years of qualifying service and is accordingly not entitled to pension. His emoluments at the time of retirement are Rs 62,000 per month. The service gratuity payable to him, at half a month's emoluments for each completed six-monthly period of qualifying service, will be:
e: Service gratuity is half a month's emoluments per completed six-monthly period. 3 years = 6 periods, so 6 x Rs 31,000 = Rs 1,86,000.

q: The last basic pay drawn by a deceased railway servant was Rs 74,000 per month. The family pension payable to his family at the normal rate, at 30 per cent of the last basic pay drawn, will be:

options.A: Rs 37,000 per month
options.B: Rs 14,800 per month
options.C: Rs 29,600 per month
options.D: Rs 22,200 per month

e: Normal rate family pension is 30 per cent of last basic pay under the RS (Pension) Rules. 30 per cent of Rs 74,000 = Rs 22,200 per month.

q: A railway servant retires on superannuation with 260 days of Leave on Average Pay at his credit. His basic pay at retirement is Rs 58,000 per month and Dearness Allowance is admissible at 50 per cent. The cash equivalent of leave salary payable to him will be:
e: Leave encashment at retirement is (pay plus DA) divided by 30, multiplied by LAP days at credit, up to 300 days. Pay plus DA = Rs 58,000 + Rs 29,000 (50 per cent) = Rs 87,000; Rs 87,000 / 30 x 260 days = Rs 7,54,000.

q: The Payment of Bonus Act, 1965 applies to every factory and to every other establishment in which the following number of persons are employed, or were employed on any day during an accounting year:

options.A: Ten or more persons
options.B: Fifty or more persons
options.C: Twenty or more persons
options.D: One hundred or more persons

e: The Payment of Bonus Act, 1965 applies under Section 1(3) to every factory and to every other establishment in which twenty or more persons are employed, or were employed on any day during an accounting year.

q: Under the Payment of Bonus Act, 1965, an 'employee' means a person employed on a salary or wage not exceeding the following amount per month:
e: Under the Payment of Bonus Act, 1965 as amended, an employee means a person employed on a salary or wage not exceeding Rs 21,000 per month; persons above that ceiling are outside the Act's bonus coverage.

q: Under Section 16 of the Payment of Bonus Act, 1965, in the case of an establishment which has been newly set up, the employees thereof are entitled to be paid bonus under the Act only when the employer derives profit from that establishment, during the first:

options.A: Three accounting years
options.B: Five accounting years
options.C: Seven accounting years
options.D: Ten accounting years

e: Section 16 of the Payment of Bonus Act, 1965 gives newly set up establishments relief: employees are entitled to bonus only when the employer derives profit from the establishment during the first five accounting years following its setting up.

q: Under Section 4(3) of the Payment of Gratuity Act, 1972, the amount of gratuity payable to an employee shall not exceed:

options.A: Rs 10 lakh
options.B: Rs 15 lakh
options.C: Rs 20 lakh
options.D: Rs 25 lakh

e: Section 4(3) of the Payment of Gratuity Act, 1972 caps the amount of gratuity payable to an employee at Rs 20 lakh.

q: Under Section 4(2) of the Payment of Gratuity Act, 1972, for every completed year of service, or part thereof in excess of six months, of an employee, the employer shall pay gratuity to him at the rate of:

options.A: Fifteen days' wages, based on the rate of wages last drawn by him
options.B: Seven days' wages, based on the rate of wages last drawn by him
options.C: Ten days' wages, based on the rate of wages last drawn by him
options.D: Twenty days' wages, based on the rate of wages last drawn by him

e: Section 4(2) of the Payment of Gratuity Act, 1972 fixes gratuity at fifteen days' wages, based on the rate of wages last drawn, for every completed year of service or part thereof in excess of six months.

q: Under Section 7(3) of the Payment of Gratuity Act, 1972, the employer is required to arrange for the payment of the amount of gratuity to the employee within the following period from the date on which it becomes payable, failing which simple interest becomes payable on it:

options.A: Fifteen days
options.B: Thirty days
options.C: Forty-five days
options.D: Sixty days

e: Section 7(3) of the Payment of Gratuity Act, 1972 requires the employer to arrange payment of gratuity within thirty days from the date it becomes payable, failing which simple interest becomes payable on it.

q: Under Section 7(2) of the Payment of Gratuity Act, 1972, in regard to the determination of the amount of gratuity payable to an employee, the correct position is that:

options.A: The employer is required to act only where the employee has filed a formal application for gratuity in writing
options.B: The amount of gratuity is determined solely by the controlling authority appointed under the Act
options.C: The employee is required to approach the controlling authority for determination of the amount in every case
options.D: The employer shall, as soon as the gratuity becomes payable, determine its amount and give notice in writing to the person to whom it is payable and also to the controlling authority, whether or not an application has been made to him

e: Section 7(2) of the Payment of Gratuity Act, 1972 obliges the employer, as soon as gratuity becomes payable, to determine its amount and give written notice to the payee and to the controlling authority, whether or not an application has been made to him.

q: Under Section 9A of the Industrial Disputes Act, 1947, an employer who proposes to effect any change in the conditions of service of workmen in respect of any matter specified in the Fourth Schedule to the Act shall not effect such change without giving the workmen likely to be affected a notice of change of:

options.A: Seven days
options.B: Fourteen days
options.C: Twenty-one days
options.D: Thirty days

e: Section 9A of the Industrial Disputes Act, 1947 bars an employer from effecting a change in conditions of service in Fourth Schedule matters without giving the affected workmen twenty-one days' notice of change.

q: Under Section 25C of the Industrial Disputes Act, 1947, a workman, other than a badli workman or a casual workman, whose name is borne on the muster rolls of an industrial establishment and who has completed not less than one year of continuous service, when laid off, is entitled to compensation for the days of lay-off, other than weekly holidays, equal to:

options.A: Twenty-five per cent of the total of his basic wages and dearness allowance
options.B: Fifty per cent of the total of his basic wages and dearness allowance
options.C: Seventy-five per cent of the total of his basic wages and dearness allowance
options.D: One hundred per cent of the total of his basic wages and dearness allowance

e: Section 25C of the Industrial Disputes Act, 1947 entitles a laid-off workman with not less than one year of continuous service, other than a badli or casual workman, to compensation equal to fifty per cent of the total of basic wages and dearness allowance for the lay-off days, excluding weekly holidays.

q: Under Section 2A of the Industrial Disputes Act, 1947, where any employer discharges, dismisses, retrenches or otherwise terminates the services of an individual workman, the position is that:

options.A: Any dispute or difference between that workman and his employer, connected with or arising out of such termination, shall be deemed to be an industrial dispute, even though no other workman or any union of workmen is a party to the dispute
options.B: Such a dispute can be treated as an industrial dispute only if it is espoused by a registered trade union of workmen
options.C: Such a dispute can be treated as an industrial dispute only if it is espoused by a majority of the workmen of the establishment
options.D: Such a dispute can never be treated as an industrial dispute, as it concerns a single workman only

e: Section 2A of the Industrial Disputes Act, 1947 deems a dispute between an individual workman and his employer, connected with discharge, dismissal, retrenchment or other termination, to be an industrial dispute even though no other workman or union is a party to it.

q: Under Section 4(1)(b) of the Employees' Compensation Act, 1923, where permanent total disablement results from an injury sustained by an employee arising out of and in the course of his employment, the amount of compensation payable is equal to the following proportion of his monthly wages, multiplied by the relevant factor, or the prescribed minimum amount, whichever is more:

options.A: Forty per cent
options.B: Fifty per cent
options.C: Sixty per cent
options.D: Ninety per cent

e: Section 4(1)(b) of the Employees' Compensation Act, 1923 fixes compensation for permanent total disablement at sixty per cent of monthly wages multiplied by the relevant factor, or the prescribed minimum amount, whichever is more.

q: In regard to a trade union of railway servants which is registered under the Trade Unions Act, 1926, the correct position under Section 14 of that Act is that:

options.A: The Societies Registration Act, 1860 applies to it in full
options.B: The Companies Act applies to it in full
options.C: The Co-operative Societies Act applies to it in full
options.D: None of the Societies Registration Act, the Co-operative Societies Act and the Companies Act applies to it

e: Section 14 of the Trade Unions Act, 1926 provides that none of the Societies Registration Act, 1860, the Co-operative Societies Act and the Companies Act applies to a registered trade union.

q: Under Section 18 of the Trade Unions Act, 1926, no suit or other legal proceeding is maintainable in any civil court against a registered trade union of railway servants, or against any of its office-bearers or members, in respect of any act done in contemplation or in furtherance of a trade dispute to which a member of the union is a party, on the ground only that:

options.A: The act was done without the prior permission of the Registrar of Trade Unions
options.B: Such act induces some other person to break a contract of employment, or that it is an interference with the trade, business or employment of some other person, or with the right of some other person to dispose of his capital or labour as he wills
options.C: The act was done during the hours of work of the member concerned
options.D: The union had not submitted its annual return to the Registrar for the preceding year

e: Section 18 of the Trade Unions Act, 1926 bars a civil suit against a registered union or its office-bearers or members for an act done in contemplation or furtherance of a trade dispute on the ground only that it induces another person to break a contract of employment or interferes with another's trade, business, employment or disposal of capital or labour.

q: Under Section 20 of the Trade Unions Act, 1926, the account books of a registered trade union of railway servants, and the list of its members, shall be open to inspection by:

options.A: The Registrar of Trade Unions only
options.B: The office-bearers of the union only
options.C: An office-bearer or member of the union, at such times as may be provided for in the rules of the union
options.D: Any member of the public, on payment of the prescribed fee

e: Section 20 of the Trade Unions Act, 1926 gives every office-bearer or member of a registered trade union the right to inspect the account books and the list of members at such times as may be provided in the rules of the union.

q: Under Section 23 of the Trade Unions Act, 1926, the name of a registered trade union of railway servants may be changed only with the consent of:

options.A: Not less than two-thirds of the total number of its members
options.B: Not less than one-half of the total number of its members
options.C: Not less than three-fourths of the total number of its members
options.D: All of its members, without exception

e: Section 23 of the Trade Unions Act, 1926 permits change of name of a registered trade union only with the consent of not less than two-thirds of the total number of its members.

q: Under Section 7A of the Factories Act, 1948, applicable to staff employed in railway workshops, the general duty cast on every occupier of a factory is to ensure, so far as is reasonably practicable:

options.A: That the profits of the factory are shared with the workers employed in it
options.B: That no worker is required to work on his weekly holiday in any circumstances
options.C: That the factory is inspected by the Chief Inspector of Factories at least once in every year
options.D: The health, safety and welfare, while they are at work in the factory, of all the workers employed in it

e: Section 7A of the Factories Act, 1948 casts a general duty on every occupier to ensure, so far as is reasonably practicable, the health, safety and welfare of all workers while they are at work in the factory.

q: Under Section 40 of the Factories Act, 1948, applicable to staff employed in railway workshops, if any part of the buildings, machinery or plant in a factory is in such a condition that it is dangerous to human life or safety, the Inspector of Factories may:

options.A: Order the immediate demolition of the building or plant concerned
options.B: Serve on the occupier or manager, in writing, an order prohibiting the use of such building, machinery or plant until it has been properly repaired or altered
options.C: Impose a fine on the occupier and permit the use to continue
options.D: Direct the workers of the factory to proceed on leave until the defect is removed

e: Section 40 of the Factories Act, 1948 empowers an Inspector, where any building, machinery or plant is dangerous to human life or safety, to serve a written order on the occupier or manager prohibiting its use until properly repaired or altered.

q: Under Section 53 of the Factories Act, 1948, applicable to staff employed in railway workshops, where a worker in a factory is deprived of any of the weekly holidays admissible to him, he becomes entitled to compensatory holidays of equal number, which shall be allowed to him:

options.A: In the same week in which the weekly holiday was lost
options.B: At any time within the calendar year
options.C: At any time within six months of the loss of the weekly holiday
options.D: Within the month in which the holidays were due to be allowed, or within the two months immediately following that month

e: Section 53 of the Factories Act, 1948 requires compensatory holidays for lost weekly holidays to be allowed within the month in which they were due, or within the two months immediately following that month.

q: Under Section 95 of the Factories Act, 1948, applicable to staff employed in railway workshops, a person who wilfully obstructs an Inspector of Factories in the exercise of any power conferred on him under the Act, or fails to produce documents or registers on demand by him, is punishable with:

options.A: Imprisonment for a term which may extend to six months, or with fine which may extend to ten thousand rupees, or with both
options.B: Fine which may extend to five hundred rupees only
options.C: Imprisonment for a term which may extend to two years only
options.D: Fine which may extend to one lakh rupees only

e: Section 95 of the Factories Act, 1948 punishes wilful obstruction of an Inspector, or failure to produce documents or registers on demand, with imprisonment up to six months, or fine up to ten thousand rupees, or both.

q: Under Section 4 of the Apprentices Act, 1961, no person shall be engaged as an apprentice to undergo apprenticeship training in a designated trade in an establishment, such as a railway workshop, unless such person, or where he is a minor, his guardian, has entered into a contract of apprenticeship with the employer, and the contract is required to be registered with:

options.A: The Registrar of Trade Unions
options.B: The Inspector of Factories
options.C: The District Employment Officer
options.D: The Apprenticeship Adviser

e: Section 4 of the Apprentices Act, 1961 requires the contract of apprenticeship to be entered into with the employer and registered with the Apprenticeship Adviser before training begins.

q: Under Section 4(1) of the Sexual Harassment of Women at Workplace (Prevention, Prohibition and Redressal) Act, 2013, every employer of a workplace is required to constitute an Internal Complaints Committee where the number of employees at the workplace is:

options.A: Five or more
options.B: Ten or more
options.C: Twenty or more
options.D: Fifty or more

e: Section 4(1) of the Sexual Harassment of Women at Workplace Act, 2013 requires every employer of a workplace with ten or more employees to constitute an Internal Complaints Committee.

q: Under the Sexual Harassment of Women at Workplace (Prevention, Prohibition and Redressal) Act, 2013, the Internal Complaints Committee is required to complete its inquiry into a complaint of sexual harassment at the workplace within a period of:

options.A: Thirty days
options.B: Sixty days
options.C: Ninety days
options.D: One hundred and twenty days

e: The Sexual Harassment of Women at Workplace Act, 2013 requires the Internal Complaints Committee to complete its inquiry into a complaint within ninety days.

q: The Central Administrative Tribunal, which adjudicates service matters of railway servants, has been constituted under:

options.A: The Administrative Tribunals Act, 1985
options.B: The Administrative Tribunals Act, 1980
options.C: The Administrative Tribunals Act, 1990
options.D: The Administrative Tribunals Act, 1995

e: The Central Administrative Tribunal, which adjudicates service matters including those of railway servants, was constituted under the Administrative Tribunals Act, 1985.

q: In regard to the railway residential accommodation allotted to a railway servant, the correct position is that:

options.A: He may sublet the accommodation to any other railway servant of his choice
options.B: He may sublet the accommodation freely, provided he intimates the fact to the allotting authority within one month
options.C: He may transfer the allotment of the accommodation in favour of a colleague on his own authority
options.D: He shall not sublet the accommodation allotted to him, and unauthorised subletting renders the allotment liable to be cancelled, besides making him liable to disciplinary action

e: Under the railway quarter allotment rules, a railway servant shall not sublet the accommodation allotted to him; unauthorised subletting renders the allotment liable to cancellation and the servant liable to disciplinary action.

q: The lump sum amount received by a retired railway servant, a Government employee, on commutation of a portion of his pension is, under Section 10(10A) of the Income-tax Act:

options.A: Taxable as salary in the year of its receipt
options.B: Wholly exempt from income-tax
options.C: Exempt only to the extent of one-third of the amount received
options.D: Exempt only to the extent of one-half of the amount received

e: Section 10(10A) of the Income-tax Act wholly exempts the lump sum received by a Government employee, including a retired railway servant, on commutation of a portion of his pension.

q: For the purpose of the grant of family pension, a member of the family of a deceased railway servant, other than the spouse, is treated as dependent and eligible only where the monthly income of that member from all sources is less than:

options.A: The minimum family pension admissible, that is, Rs 5,000 per month, plus dearness relief admissible thereon
options.B: The minimum family pension admissible, that is, Rs 7,000 per month, plus dearness relief admissible thereon
options.C: The minimum family pension admissible, that is, Rs 9,000 per month, plus dearness relief admissible thereon
options.D: The minimum family pension admissible, that is, Rs 12,000 per month, plus dearness relief admissible thereon

e: For family pension, a family member other than the spouse is treated as dependent only if monthly income from all sources is less than the minimum family pension, which is Rs 9,000 per month, plus dearness relief admissible thereon.

q: Under the Employees' Compensation Act, 1923, where an employee employed in an employment specified in Schedule III to the Act contracts an occupational disease peculiar to that employment, the contracting of the disease is treated as:

options.A: An injury by accident arising out of, and in the course of, his employment
options.B: An ordinary illness, for which no compensation is admissible under the Act
options.C: An injury for which compensation is admissible only where the employer admits his liability
options.D: An injury for which compensation is admissible only where the disease results in the death of the employee

e: Under the Employees' Compensation Act, 1923, contracting an occupational disease listed in Schedule III, peculiar to the employment, is treated as an injury by accident arising out of and in the course of employment, making compensation admissible.

q: Under Section 2(a) of the Industrial Disputes Act, 1947, in relation to an industry carried on by or under the authority of the Railway Department, the 'appropriate Government' for the purposes of the Act is:

options.A: The State Government in which the headquarters of the railway servant is situated
options.B: The Railway Board
options.C: The Ministry of Labour and Employment, acting as an appellate authority
options.D: The Central Government

e: Section 2(a) of the Industrial Disputes Act, 1947 makes the Central Government the appropriate Government for an industry carried on by or under the authority of a department of the Central Government, which includes the Railway Department.

q: Under Section 17 of the Trade Unions Act, 1926, no office-bearer or member of a registered trade union of railway servants shall be liable to punishment for criminal conspiracy, in respect of an agreement made between the members for the purpose of furthering any of the legitimate objects of the union, unless:

options.A: The agreement was not reduced to writing
options.B: The agreement is an agreement to commit an offence
options.C: The agreement was made without the consent of the Registrar of Trade Unions
options.D: The agreement was made during a period when a trade dispute was in progress

e: Section 17 of the Trade Unions Act, 1926 protects office-bearers and members from punishment for criminal conspiracy for agreements furthering legitimate objects of the union, unless the agreement is an agreement to commit an offence.

q: Under Section 88 of the Factories Act, 1948, applicable to staff employed in railway workshops, the manager of a factory is required to send a notice, in the prescribed form, to the prescribed authority where an accident in the factory causes death, or causes any bodily injury by reason of which the person injured is prevented from working for a period of:

options.A: Twelve hours or more after the occurrence of the accident
options.B: Twenty-four hours or more after the occurrence of the accident
options.C: Forty-eight hours or more after the occurrence of the accident
options.D: Seventy-two hours or more after the occurrence of the accident

e: Section 88 of the Factories Act, 1948 requires notice of an accident causing death, or bodily injury preventing the person from working for forty-eight hours or more after the accident, to be sent to the prescribed authority in the prescribed form.

q: Under Section 25B of the Industrial Disputes Act, 1947, a workman is deemed to be in continuous service for a period of one year under an employer if, during the period of twelve calendar months preceding the date with reference to which the calculation is to be made, he has actually worked under the employer for not less than:

options.A: 240 days, in a case other than employment in an underground mine
options.B: 190 days, in a case other than employment in an underground mine
options.C: 180 days, in a case other than employment in an underground mine
options.D: 300 days, in a case other than employment in an underground mine

e: Section 25B of the Industrial Disputes Act, 1947 deems a workman in continuous service for one year if he has actually worked not less than 240 days in the preceding twelve calendar months, in a case other than employment in an underground mine, where the figure is 190 days.

q: Under Section 2(m) of the Factories Act, 1948, the premises which are NOT included within the meaning of a 'factory' for the purposes of the Act are:

options.A: A mine subject to the operation of the Mines Act
options.B: A railway running shed
options.C: A mobile unit belonging to the Armed Forces of the Union
options.D: All of the above

e: Section 2(m) of the Factories Act, 1948 excludes from the definition of factory a mine under the Mines Act, a mobile unit belonging to the Armed Forces of the Union, and a railway running shed, so all three listed premises are excluded.

q: Under Section 10 of the Industrial Disputes Act, 1947, an industrial dispute is adjudicated upon by a Labour Court, an Industrial Tribunal or a National Tribunal where:

options.A: The parties to the dispute directly approach the Tribunal for adjudication
options.B: The appropriate Government, being of the opinion that an industrial dispute exists or is apprehended, refers the dispute to the Court or Tribunal for adjudication
options.C: The Registrar of Trade Unions certifies the dispute for adjudication
options.D: The employer alone applies to the Tribunal for adjudication of the dispute

e: Section 10 of the Industrial Disputes Act, 1947 provides for adjudication by a Labour Court, Industrial Tribunal or National Tribunal only when the appropriate Government, being of the opinion that an industrial dispute exists or is apprehended, refers it for adjudication.

q: Under Section 12 of the Employees' Compensation Act, 1923, where an employer, in the course of or for the purpose of his business, contracts with a contractor for the execution of any work, and an employee employed by the contractor sustains personal injury by accident, the compensation is in the first instance payable by the principal employer, and in that event, the principal employer is entitled to:

options.A: Recover the amount from the wages of the injured employee
options.B: Recover the amount from the Employees' State Insurance Corporation
options.C: Be indemnified by the contractor in respect of the compensation so paid by him
options.D: No recovery of the amount from any person whatsoever

e: Section 12 of the Employees' Compensation Act, 1923 makes the principal employer liable in the first instance for compensation to a contractor's employee injured on the contracted work, and entitles the principal employer to be indemnified by the contractor.

q: Under Rule 8 of the Railway Services (Conduct) Rules, 1966, relating to connection with the press and other media, a railway servant shall not, except with the previous sanction of the Government:

options.A: Own, wholly or in part, or conduct, or participate in the editing or management of, any newspaper or other periodical publication, or electronic media
options.B: Read any newspaper or periodical publication during his hours of duty
options.C: Subscribe to any newspaper or periodical publication in his own name
options.D: Make any statement to a representative of the press, even in the performance of his official duties

e: Rule 8 of the RS (Conduct) Rules, 1966 bars a railway servant, except with previous sanction of the Government, from owning wholly or in part, conducting, or participating in the editing or management of any newspaper, periodical publication or electronic media.

q: Under the Payment of Bonus Act, 1965, the 'allocable surplus' available for distribution as bonus among the employees of an employer, other than a banking company, is:

options.A: Sixty-seven per cent of the available surplus in an accounting year
options.B: Fifty per cent of the available surplus in an accounting year
options.C: Seventy-five per cent of the available surplus in an accounting year
options.D: Sixty per cent of the available surplus in an accounting year

e: Section 2(4) of the Payment of Bonus Act, 1965 defines allocable surplus as 67 per cent of available surplus only for the specified company case that has not made the prescribed dividend arrangements, and 60 per cent in any other case, which covers an employer other than a banking company in the general case.

q: Under Section 4(5) of the Payment of Gratuity Act, 1972, the provisions of the Act do not affect the right of an employee to:

options.A: Claim gratuity twice over, once under the Act and again under his service rules
options.B: Receive better terms of gratuity under any award, or agreement, or contract with his employer
options.C: Claim gratuity even before completing one year of service in every case
options.D: Claim gratuity at a rate higher than that laid down in the Act, as of right

e: Section 4(5) of the Payment of Gratuity Act, 1972 preserves the employee's right to receive better terms of gratuity under any award, agreement or contract with the employer; the Act sets a floor, not a ceiling on better terms.

q: Under the Sexual Harassment of Women at Workplace (Prevention, Prohibition and Redressal) Act, 2013, a complaint of sexual harassment at a workplace can be made to the Internal Complaints Committee by:

options.A: A woman employed at the workplace only
options.B: A woman employed at the workplace only, and not by a woman who has died
options.C: A woman employee of the same office in which the respondent is employed only
options.D: An aggrieved woman, that is, a woman of any age, whether employed at the workplace or not, who alleges to have been subjected to an act of sexual harassment at the workplace

e: Under the Sexual Harassment of Women at Workplace Act, 2013, an aggrieved woman means a woman of any age, whether employed at the workplace or not, who alleges sexual harassment at the workplace, and she can complain to the Internal Complaints Committee.

q: In regard to appointment on compassionate grounds on the Railways of a married daughter of a deceased railway servant, the correct position is that:

options.A: She may be considered for such appointment, provided she was dependent on the deceased railway servant at the time of his death and fulfils the prescribed conditions, including that she will maintain the other dependent members of the family
options.B: She can never be considered for such appointment, as a married daughter ceases to be a member of the family
options.C: She may be considered only where the deceased railway servant has left behind no other member of his family
options.D: She may be considered only where she has been appointed on the Railways earlier on a temporary basis

e: On the Railways, a married daughter of a deceased railway servant may be considered for compassionate appointment if she was dependent on the deceased at the time of death, fulfils the prescribed conditions, and undertakes to maintain the other dependent family members.

q: A railway servant dies while in service after completing 13 years of qualifying service. His emoluments at the time of death are Rs 51,000 per month. The death gratuity payable to his family will be:
e: For death with 11 to 20 years of service, the death gratuity slab is 20 times emoluments. Here service is 13 years, so gratuity = 20 x Rs 51,000 = Rs 10,20,000.

q: A railway servant retires from service after completing 26 years of qualifying service. His emoluments at the time of retirement are Rs 44,000 per month. The retirement gratuity payable to him will be:
e: Retirement gratuity is one-fourth of emoluments per completed six-monthly period. 26 years = 52 periods, so 52 x Rs 11,000 (one-fourth of Rs 44,000) = Rs 5,72,000, within the 16.5 times maximum.

q: A railway servant retires from service after rendering only 2 years of qualifying service and is accordingly not entitled to pension. His emoluments at the time of retirement are Rs 66,000 per month. The service gratuity payable to him will be:
e: Service gratuity is half a month's emoluments per completed six-monthly period. 2 years = 4 periods, so 4 x Rs 33,000 = Rs 1,32,000.

q: A railway servant dies while in service after completing 10 months of qualifying service. His emoluments at the time of death are Rs 72,000 per month. The death gratuity payable to his family will be:
e: For death within one year of service, the death gratuity slab is 2 times emoluments. Here service is 10 months, so gratuity = 2 x Rs 72,000 = Rs 1,44,000.

q: The last basic pay drawn by a deceased railway servant was Rs 38,000 per month. The family pension payable to his family at the normal rate, at 30 per cent of the last basic pay drawn, will be:

options.A: Rs 7,600 per month
options.B: Rs 11,400 per month
options.C: Rs 19,000 per month
options.D: Rs 15,200 per month

e: Normal rate family pension is 30 per cent of last basic pay. 30 per cent of Rs 38,000 = Rs 11,400 per month.

q: A railway servant retires on superannuation with 200 days of Leave on Average Pay at his credit. His basic pay at retirement is Rs 52,000 per month and Dearness Allowance is admissible at 50 per cent. The cash equivalent of leave salary payable to him will be:
e: Leave encashment is (pay plus DA) divided by 30, multiplied by LAP days at credit. Pay plus DA = Rs 52,000 + Rs 26,000 (50 per cent) = Rs 78,000; Rs 78,000 / 30 x 200 days = Rs 5,20,000.

q: A settlement arrived at in the course of conciliation proceedings under the Industrial Disputes Act, 1947 is binding on:

options.A: Only those workmen who were parties to the settlement
options.B: Only the employer who has signed the settlement
options.C: All parties to the industrial dispute and all workmen employed in the establishment, as provided in the Act
options.D: No person, as a settlement has only an advisory value

e: Under Section 18 of the Industrial Disputes Act, 1947, a settlement arrived at in the course of conciliation proceedings is binding on all parties to the dispute and on all workmen employed in the establishment, including those who join later, as provided in the Act.

q: Under the National Pension System, the Central Recordkeeping Agency is responsible for:

options.A: Recordkeeping of subscribers' accounts and issuance of the Permanent Retirement Account Number
options.B: Investing the contributions of subscribers in the securities market
options.C: Fixing the rates of pension payable to subscribers
options.D: Selling annuity policies to subscribers on their exit

e: Under the National Pension System, the Central Recordkeeping Agency keeps records of subscribers' accounts, maintains the subscriber database and issues the Permanent Retirement Account Number; investment is done by pension fund managers and annuities by annuity service providers.

q: Under Section 33 of the Industrial Disputes Act, 1947, during the pendency of conciliation or adjudication proceedings in respect of an industrial dispute, the employer shall not, in regard to any matter connected with the dispute:

options.A: Declare a lock-out in any circumstances whatsoever
options.B: Alter the conditions of service of the workmen concerned in the dispute, or discharge, dismiss or punish any such workman for a misconduct connected with the dispute, except with the express permission in writing of the authority before which the proceeding is pending
options.C: Engage any new workman in the establishment
options.D: Transfer any workman from the establishment to any other station

e: Section 33 of the Industrial Disputes Act, 1947 bars the employer, during pendency of conciliation or adjudication proceedings, from altering service conditions in a matter connected with the dispute, or discharging, dismissing or punishing a workman for misconduct connected with the dispute, except with express written permission of the authority before which the proceeding is pending.

q: As a result of the Constitution (Forty-second Amendment) Act, in a departmental inquiry against a railway servant, the position regarding the proposed penalty is that:

options.A: The charged servant must be given a second opportunity to represent against the penalty proposed, after the inquiry is completed
options.B: The charged servant has no right to make a representation against the proposed penalty at the post-inquiry stage, the earlier opportunity to defend himself during the inquiry being sufficient
options.C: No departmental inquiry is required at all before imposing a major penalty
options.D: The right of appeal against the penalty stands abolished

e: After the Constitution (Forty-second Amendment), the charged Government servant has no right to a second opportunity to represent against the proposed penalty at the post-inquiry stage; the opportunity to defend himself during the inquiry is sufficient, though he still gets a copy of the inquiry report and can appeal.
